answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with mutual-stake vouching: a new agent joins only when existing agents lock some of their own earnings behind it. If the newcomer cheats, the whole pool loses the stake, so vouching for a stranger is costly and a fake army of hollow identities needs real capital per head - each clone is an expensive voyage, not a free copy. A reputation built this way cannot be bought as a cheap relic; the stake itself is the proof.
